FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Fourth Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Ferro Alloys Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first issued in 1960 and was subsequently revised in 1964, 1981 and 1990. In view of the experience gained during these years, it was felt necessary to revise this standard. The following main modifications have been made in this revision: a) b) Number of grades have been increased from seven to eight. and modified keeping in view the prevalent

Chemical composition of all the grades has been rationalized practice and demand of industry.

For the purpose of deciding whether observed or calculated, expressing IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off the rounded off value should be the

a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in same as that of the specified value in this standard.

The content of the main constituent of the melts (or parts of continuous taps) constituting the consignment may vary between the minimum and maximum limits, specified for the appropriate ferrotitanium designation. 3.3 Ferrotitanium A master alloy of iron and titanium with a minimum titanium content of 20.0 percent by mass and a maximum titanium content of 75.0 percent by mass obtained by reduction. 4 GRADES This standard covers eight grades of ferrotitanium, specified in Table 1. 5 PARTICULARS ORDERING TO BE SPECIFIED as

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, definitions shall apply. 3.1 Cast (Melt) The product of any of the following: a) b) c) One furnace heat, or One tap of continuous furnace, or A number of furnace or crucible heats of similar composition mixed in a ladle or holding furnace and used for making a cast. of Consignment the following

3.2 Constitution

3.2.1 Tupped Lot Method A consignment constituted consists of a ferrotitanium part of a continuous tap). 3.2.2 Graded Lot Method A consignment constituted by the graded lot method consists of a number of melts (or parts of continuous taps) of one ferrotitanium designation. The ferrotitanium content of the melts (or parts of continuous taps) constiiuring the consignment shall not differ from each other by ~more than 3 percent. 3.2.3 Bletldcd Lot Method by the tapped lot method mass of one melt (or one 6 SUPPLY

7.2.2 If specified by the purchaser at the time of enquiry and order that each lump of the batch should conform to the chemical composition specified in Table 1, this shall be agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer.
NOTE -The material belonging to a cast (melt) which is out of specification, shall not be blended or mixed with the material of another cast/melt.

MUX

Over

Undersize shall not include dust ( - 2 mm).

7.2.3 The chemical composition given in Table 1 shows only the main constituent elements and usual impurities. If the purchaser requires closer ranges for the main element contents and/or different limits for specified elements and/or non-specified elements, this shall be agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 7.2.4 The chemical composition of the material shall be determined either by the method specified in IS 1559 or any other established instrumental/chemical method. In case of dispute, the procedure given in the latest version of IS 1559 shall be the referee method. However, where the method is not given in IS 1559, the referee method shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 8 SIZE Unless otherwise specified. the material shall be supplied in lumps or as crushed and screened particles. The particle size ranges and tolerances shall be as given in Table 2. The undersize vaLues shall be valid at the point of delivery to the purchaser.

9 EXTRANEOUS

CONTAMINATIONS

The material shall be reasonably free from extraneous contaminations, namely, slag and non-metallic inclusions, etc. 10 SAMPLING 10.1 Each batch of the material chemical analysis in accordance shall be sampled for with IS 1472.

10.2 For size determination sampling shall be carried out as agreed to between manufacturer and purchaser at the time of enquiry and order. 11 PACKING The material shall be packed in suitable containers, in quantities as mutually agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser. 12 MARKING 12.1 The container shall be marked with the following: a) b) Supplier's name or trade-mark; cast or lot number;
